implementation_notes: The default C++ realization keeps the GoF roles literal: an abstract Component declares the virtual operations, leaf classes override them, and a container stores std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Component>> and forwards the operation to each child. unique_ptr encodes the tree's single-ownership invariant in the type system, so a node cannot be owned twice; the base needs a virtual destructor or deleting through a base pointer is undefined behaviour. Use this form when node kinds are open (plugins, external code) or when nodes are long-lived objects with identity; prefer the std::variant variant when the node set is closed and the tree is traversed heavily.
pitfalls: A missing virtual destructor on Component makes unique_ptr<Component> delete through the base pointer undefined behaviour.
Child management on the Component interface forces leaves into no-op add/remove stubs; keep it on the container and downcast at the few sites that edit structure.
unique_ptr children cannot be shared: if two parents need the same subtree the structure is a DAG and needs a shared-ownership variant.

variants.name: Closed node set as std::variant visited with std::visit (value semantics)
variants.implementation_notes: When the node kinds are fixed at compile time, a std::variant of those kinds replaces the class hierarchy: nodes are held by value, dispatch is std::visit over a jump table, and a visitor that does not handle an alternative fails to compile, so exhaustiveness is enforced by the compiler rather than by discipline. Recursive alternatives still need indirection - a variant cannot contain itself - so the container's children are boxed (std::unique_ptr or a small deep-copying box type). Choose this for ASTs, expression trees and render trees that are built and traversed often; keep the virtual form when third-party code must add node kinds.
pitfalls: A variant cannot contain itself: the recursive alternative must be boxed or the type is ill-formed.
Adding a node kind breaks every std::visit without a matching overload - that is the guarantee, but it means one edit per traversal site.
std::visit over several variants generates an N-ary dispatch table; keep the alternative count modest or code size grows quickly.

variants.name: shared_ptr children for shared subtrees and DAGs
variants.idiom_name: std::shared_ptr<Component> child collections with weak_ptr parent links
variants.implementation_notes: When the same subtree legitimately appears under several parents - a DAG rather than a tree - children are held as std::shared_ptr<Component>: shared ownership keeps a shared node alive while any parent references it, at the cost of an atomic reference count per node and the loss of the single-owner invariant. Back-pointers must be std::weak_ptr, because a child holding a shared_ptr to its parent keeps the entire structure alive. Reach for this deliberately; for a genuine tree the unique_ptr form is smaller, faster and easier to reason about.
pitfalls: shared_ptr cycles: parent and child holding each other keep the structure alive forever; use weak_ptr for the back edge.
Copying a node with shared_ptr children aliases the subtree - deep copies require an explicit clone operation.
Per-node control blocks and atomic refcounts cost more than the unique_ptr tree, and const-correctness suffers because shared_ptr propagates constness only to the pointer.
